notes: The times on the messages themselves are story times now. The little stamp under a bubble and the one on each row of the chat list were still reading the real clock — the hour you happened to be holding the phone — while everything else about a conversation had moved onto the story's calendar. They now read the same clock the characters do: a bubble shows the story time it was said at, with AM or PM rather than the old twenty-four hour form, and a chat row shows the time if it happened today in the story, the weekday if it was earlier this week, and the date beyond that. Because they are measured against the story clock rather than a fixed one, moving time forward re-labels them: a conversation that read 9:07 AM this morning reads Thu once the story has moved on to Sunday.
